25.6 Current Candle ON, Extended Hours OFF — why

Setting v1 value Effect [TS] Why for v1
Current Candle ON The forming candle is used as if closed; OFF = last closed candle Candidates appear in real time instead of up to 5 minutes late
Ext. Hours OFF Pre/post-market data excluded from calculations v1 trades the regular session; pre-market data would distort VWAP, EMAs and RVOL

Side effect of Current Candle ON: results can change within the same 5 minutes. A stock may appear at 10:02 and disappear at 10:04. That is normal. The scanner is a candidate finder; the alert (evaluated on closed candles) is the trigger.

26.1 The v1 candidate workflow

S&P 500 (~500 symbols)
   │  Market Scanner (bullish / bearish), ~9:40+ and refreshed periodically
   ▼
Scanner results (e.g. 5–40 names)
   │  Candidate ranking (Chapter 15)
   ▼
Static lists: RB v1 LONG <date> (≤10) · RB v1 SHORT <date> (≤10)
   │  Multi-Factor Alerts on each symbol (manually or via Sidekick)
   ▼
Alert fires → inspect → (maybe) paper trade

Why static lists need refreshing daily (or intraday): a stock that qualified at 9:45 may be flat by 11:00, and fresh movers appear. Alerts attach to symbols: an alert on yesterday’s candidate keeps firing on yesterday’s idea. Rebuild the lists every morning, review them around 11:00 and 13:30, and delete or let expire the alerts on dropped names.

27 Sidekick — TrendSpider’s AI Assistant

27.1 What Sidekick is [TS]

Sidekick is an AI chat assistant inside TrendSpider. It works from TrendSpider’s own data and, with your permission, your account content (charts, watchlists, backtests). Key facts:

Capability / limit Detail
Can do Build, run, save and schedule scans; create and organise watchlists (including from scan results); build Multi-Factor Alerts for one ticker or a whole watchlist; add basic chart annotations; write custom indicators
Alert creation limit ~20 tickers per message (soft limit)
Analysis limit ~15–20 tickers at once; use a scan for larger lists
Data it reads Price data, fundamentals, filings, earnings call transcripts, analyst estimates, options flow, short volume, insider activity, your chart, your broker holdings if SignalStack is connected (read-only)
Cannot Browse the internet; place, modify or close trades
News A news feed is not listed among its data sources → VERIFY before relying on it for news risk
Messages 25 free messages per calendar month on every plan; paid Sidekick packages add more
Confirmation step The documentation does not describe an approval step before it acts → assume it acts immediately

SAFETY WARNING — Sidekick can change your account

Sidekick can create alerts, scans and watchlists. A vague prompt like “set alerts on my list” could create alerts on the wrong list, with the wrong conditions, or use up your alert capacity. Before large actions:

  1. Ask it first to describe what it will do (“Show me the exact conditions and symbols you would use; do not create anything yet”).
  2. Check the list name, timeframe and every condition against this manual.
  3. Then ask it to execute.
  4. Afterwards, open 2–3 created alerts and verify them manually.

27.2 Prompt structure: Action + Scope + Filters + Output [TS]

Part Meaning Example
Action What to do “Scan”, “Rank”, “Set alerts”, “Add to watchlist”
Scope The universe “my watchlist RB v1 LONG 2026-10-29”, “S&P 500”
Filters Conditions “5m RSI14 between 55 and 70”
Output Format “Table, top 10, columns: …”

27.3 Ready-to-copy prompts

1. Rank bullish candidates

Rank the symbols in my saved scan "RB v1 – Regular-Session Bullish Momentum"
(regular session only). For each, using the 5-minute chart, report: RVOL(20),
RSI(14), % distance of close from VWAP, (EMA9-EMA20)/price in %, 5m ATR(14),
distance from VWAP in ATR units, today's % change vs prior close, and whether
the 15-minute close is above a rising EMA20. Prefer RSI 55-70, RVOL 2-6,
VWAP distance 0.2-1.5 ATR, daily change +1% to +4%. Flag anything with RSI > 78,
RVOL > 10, or more than 2.5 ATR above VWAP as "overextended". Output a table
sorted best to worst, top 10. Do not create or modify anything.

2. Rank bearish candidates

Same as before but for "RB v1 – Regular-Session Bearish Momentum": prefer
RSI 30-45, price 0.2-1.5 ATR below VWAP, EMA9 below EMA20, daily change -1% to
-4%, 15-minute close below a falling EMA20. Flag RSI < 22, RVOL > 10, or more
than 2.5 ATR below VWAP. Also flag any stock down 10% or more from the prior
close (possible short-sale restriction). Top 10 table. Do not create anything.

3. Create static watchlists

Create a new watchlist named "RB v1 LONG <YYYY-MM-DD>" containing exactly these
symbols: <SYM1>, <SYM2>, ... Then show me the list contents. Do not add
alerts.

4. Why does a stock qualify?

On <SYMBOL>, regular session only: show the latest closed 5-minute candle's
open, high, low, close, volume, VWAP(14,0,HLC3), EMA9, EMA20, RSI14, RVOL(20,SMA)
and the latest 15-minute close and EMA20. For each RB v1 LONG condition
(close>VWAP, EMA9>EMA20, RSI>55, RVOL>1.5, close>open, 15m close>EMA20) say
TRUE/FALSE with the numbers.

5. Compare candidates

Compare <SYM1> and <SYM2> for an RB v1 LONG setup on the 5-minute chart:
extension from VWAP in ATR units, RSI, RVOL, EMA separation, nearest resistance
above (prior day high, today's high), and earnings date. Which has more room to
reach a 2R target from a break of the last candle's high? Table format.

6. Create alerts across a watchlist (two-step)

STEP 1 (preview only): For each symbol in watchlist "RB v1 LONG <date>",
describe the Multi-Factor Alert you would create: name "RB v1 – LONG Setup",
ALL of: 5m Close > VWAP(14,0,HLC3); 5m EMA(9) > EMA(20); 5m RSI(14) > 55;
5m Relative Volume(20, SMA) > 1.5; 5m Close > Open; 15m Close > EMA(20).
Regular session only (no extended hours). Expire at end of today. Do NOT create
yet - list the symbols and conditions.

Then, after checking: STEP 2: Create exactly those alerts. (≤ 20 symbols per message.)

7. Review overextension

For each symbol in "RB v1 LONG <date>", compute how many 5m ATRs price is above
VWAP and above the 5m EMA20, and count consecutive green 5-minute candles.
Mark "extended" if > 2.5 ATR above VWAP or > 5 consecutive green candles.

8. News / earnings risk

For each symbol in "RB v1 LONG <date>" and "RB v1 SHORT <date>": list the next
earnings date and flag any reporting today after the close or tomorrow before
the open. Note any data you have on unusual activity today. State clearly if
you do not have news data.

9. Analyse an alert after it fires

My "RB v1 – LONG Setup" alert fired on <SYMBOL> at <HH:MM> ET. Using the
5-minute candle that closed at that time as the signal candle: give its high,
low, range, range vs 5m ATR(14), distance of close from VWAP in ATR, RSI, RVOL,
and the 15m condition. Compute entry = high + $0.02, stop = low,
risk/share, shares = floor(250 / risk) and also floor(50000 / entry), the
smaller of the two, and the 2R target. Note any nearby resistance within 2R.
Do not create anything.

COMMON MISTAKE

Treating Sidekick’s numbers as authoritative. It is a language model. Spot-check any value you will trade on directly on your chart, especially entry, stop and size.

28 Multi-Factor Alerts — RB v1 LONG and SHORT

28.1 Facts that shape alert design [TS]

Fact Consequence
The lowest alert timeframe is 5 minutes v1 fits exactly; you cannot alert on 1m
An alert is checked when the candle of its smallest timeframe closes Alert fires just after each 5m close; the signal candle is complete
Larger-timeframe conditions use the last calculated value and can become untrue when that candle closes Re-check the 15m chart manually
Extended-hours data is only used if Use Extended Hours is ticked; that unlocks Fire During (Market hours / Extended session / Pre-Market / Post Market) v1: leave unticked
Expiration sets how long it stays active and how many times it can fire; whichever comes first cancels it. Expiration counts calendar days Choose deliberately
Create Alert applies to the ticker currently open Alerts attach to symbols
Alerts are delivered via email, SMS, webhook (and the mobile app) Chapter 29
The Alerts FAQ documents a soft limit of 20 alerts per Sidekick message Batch by 20

28.2 Screen-by-screen: building “RB v1 – LONG Setup”

TRENDSPIDER STEP — Create the LONG alert [TS]

  1. Load the symbol (e.g., AAPL) on any timeframe.
  2. Click the vertical ellipsis (⋮) next to Alerts & Bots in the top toolbar → Multi-Factor Alert.
  3. Choose Skip to Point & Click Editor.
  4. Chart Type: Generic OHLC (candles).
  5. Alert Name: RB v1 – LONG Setup (the symbol is appended automatically).
  6. Your Note: Inspect only. Entry = break of signal high + buffer; stop = signal low; 0.25% risk; 2R. Leave it plain text: JSON here is sent to a configured webhook.
  7. Expiration: see the table below.
  8. Extended Market Hours / Use Extended Hours: unticked.
  9. Conditions: add parameter here → Condition, six times, all in one group set to All of the following:
# Timeframe Condition Candle reference
1 5 min Close is above VWAP (14, 0, HLC3) Happened (current)
2 5 min EMA (9) is above EMA (20) Happened
3 5 min RSI (14) is above 55 Happened
4 5 min Relative Volume (20, SMA, base 1) is above 1.5 Happened
5 5 min Close is above Open Happened
6 15 min Close is above EMA (20) Happened
  1. Leave each condition on Happened (the default: the exact candle) rather than Happened Within N candles [TS].
  2. Click Create Alert.

RECOMMENDATION — Test notifications before your first session

TrendSpider’s notification page does not document a “send test” button. Do it during market hours: if the alert is not set to use extended hours, it is checked during the regular session.

30 The Position Tool

30.1 What it is

A drawing tool that marks an entry, a stop and a target on the chart as shaded risk/reward zones. You use it to see whether a trade makes sense before placing it.

VERIFY — limited official documentation

TrendSpider’s official source located for the Position Tool is an older blog release note. It states the tool is in the left drawing toolbar (second from the bottom at that time), hotkey ALT+P; right-click → properties to edit colours, labels and enter exact levels; and right-click to add an alert to any of its levels. Whether it currently displays share quantity or an R:R ratio was not confirmed. Capture SS-30/31 and update this section.

30.2 How to use it before a paper trade

  1. After the alert, identify the signal candle.
  2. Select the Position Tool (ALT+P, or from the left toolbar) and draw it from the entry level.
  3. Right-click → properties → type exact levels:
    • LONG: Entry = signal high + buffer; Stop = signal low; Target = Entry + 2 × (Entry − Stop).
    • SHORT: Entry = signal low − buffer; Stop = signal high; Target = Entry − 2 × (Stop − Entry).
  4. Look at the chart: is there resistance (LONG) or support (SHORT) inside the green zone? If yes → Do-Not-Take item 5.
  5. Optional: add alerts on the stop and target levels as a back-up reminder.
  6. Use the Share Chart Tool to capture this “before” screenshot for your journal.

31.1 What the Strategy Tester can and cannot do [TS]

Feature Supported?
Access Strategy Tester button, bottom-left; opens below the chart; Maximize toggle top-right
Strategy settings Name, Timeframe (only one per strategy), Depth (candles or date range, limited by plan), Settings: chart type, extended hours on/off, direction (long or short), trade cost (%)

Partial exits / scaling in No. Any exit closes 100%; no consecutive entries
Long + short in one strategy No. Build separate strategies
Multiple timeframes Not with traditional indicators (FAQ). Approximate with custom indicators
Export Arrow button → Download Test Results (CSV/TSV)
Run / Save Run; Save after every change
Backtest depth by plan (pricing page) Min backtest timeframe and depth vary by plan, e.g., 5 min / 10K candles on Premium

31.2 The closest possible v1 backtest

Strategy “RB v1 LONG – approx”: Timeframe 5 min, Settings: Ext. Hours off, Direction Long, Trade cost e.g. 0.02% (a slippage/fee allowance [REC]).

Entry (Script, All of):

v1 condition Strategy Tester version Exact?
Close > VWAP Close > VWAP(14, 0, HLC3) ✓
EMA9 > EMA20 EMA(9) > EMA(20) ✓
RSI14 > 55 RSI(14) > 55 ✓
RVOL20 > 1.5 Relative Volume(20) > 1.5 ✓
Close > Open Close > Open ✓
15m Close > EMA20 Approximation: 5m Close > EMA(60) on the 5m chart (≈ 20 × 15-minute bars of time) ✗ approximation
Scanner filters (S&P 500, price, daily +1%, Daily Vol MA) Run the test per symbol on a list of liquid S&P 500 names; the daily +1% filter cannot be reproduced on a single 5m timeframe ✗
Entry on break of signal high within 1–2 candles Tester enters on the signal; it cannot express “next candle trades above this candle’s high” without custom scripting ✗

Exits:

v1 exit Strategy Tester version Exact?
A: stop = signal-candle low Stop Loss in ATR units (e.g., 1 × ATR) as a proxy, or a Script exit “Close < Low 1 candle ago” (approximate) ✗ approximation
B: 2R Take Profit = 2 × the stop distance (e.g., Stop 1 xATR, Take Profit 2 xATR) ≈ (R defined by ATR, not candle)
C: trend failure Script exit: Close < VWAP OR EMA(9) crossed below EMA(20), After candle closes ✓ ✓
D: time stop # Candles Passed = 6 (exits regardless of +0.5R; the tester cannot condition on MFE) ✗ approximation

Build “RB v1 SHORT – approx” separately with Direction Short and all conditions mirrored.

WHAT THE BACKTEST CANNOT TELL YOU

Because the 15m filter, the daily filter, the breakout entry and the candle-based stop are approximated, the backtest measures a cousin of v1, not v1 itself. Use it to answer directional questions (“does the trend-failure exit help?”, “is a 2R target better than 1.5R?”), not to predict v1’s P/L. Your paper-trading journal is the primary evidence.

31.3 Interpreting results

Metric Question it answers Caution
Number of trades Is the sample large enough? < 100 trades = little statistical meaning
Win rate How often it wins Meaningless without average win/loss
Average win/loss, profit factor Is the payoff sufficient? Chapter 39
Max drawdown Worst peak-to-trough Will you tolerate it?
Equity curve vs Buy & Hold (grey) Smooth vs lumpy One big winner can hide many losers
Price Behavior Explorer Price change vs candles since entry Useful for the time-stop question

31.4 Avoiding overfitting

  • Decide the parameters before testing; change one thing per test.
  • Test on one period (e.g., Jan–Jun), then confirm on a different period (Jul–Oct) without changing anything.
  • Prefer round, simple values (RSI 55, not 56.3).
  • If small parameter changes swing results wildly, the edge is not robust.

PART VI — PAPER EXECUTION (LEVEL 6)

32 Paper Trading Architecture

Component Role What it is NOT
TrendSpider Analysis, scanners, alerts, and a manual order ticket (Trading widget) Not a broker. It “can not place orders in your brokerage account” by itself [TS]
SignalStack Order router between TrendSpider and your broker [SS] Not a broker. It does not hold your money
Alpaca Paper Simulated brokerage account [ALP] Not real money. Fills are simulated

NO REAL MONEY IN PAPER MODE

In v1, every order goes to the Alpaca PAPER account. Paper accounts start with $100,000 of simulated money [ALP]. Before every order, confirm that the Trading widget shows the paper account (Chapter 35).

33 SignalStack

33.1 What it does [SS]

SignalStack converts signals from charting platforms (TrendSpider, TradingView, etc.) into orders at a connected broker or exchange. TrendSpider’s Trading widget uses it as the plumbing: when you press Submit in TrendSpider, SignalStack transmits the order to Alpaca. TrendSpider states that routing typically takes about 0.3 s, and rarely up to 12 s for some brokers [TS].

33.2 Key concepts

Concept Detail
Broker connection Connect Alpaca once, under Brokers & Webhooks [SS]
Paper vs live accounts After connecting a broker, its accounts (live or paper) are fetched automatically [SS]
Signal “A trade order successfully sent to a linked broker account”. Errors don’t count; “sent” ≠ “executed” [SS pricing]
Quota Free plan: 5 signals/month with unlimited paper signals. Paid tiers: Basic 50, Premium 250, Pro 1,000/month. Unused signals don’t roll over [SS pricing, 2026-10-28]
TrendSpider allowance TrendSpider’s pricing page lists 5 free automated trades per month with discounted access beyond that. VERIFY whether manual widget orders to a paper account count against anything
Webhooks SignalStack can receive alerts via webhook (JSON in TrendSpider’s “Your Note” field) for automated trading [SS]

33.3 Why webhook automation is NOT part of v1

  1. The alert is not the trade. v1 requires human confirmation: checklist, break of the signal candle, risk check.
  2. Errors scale. A mis-built webhook alert fires orders on every symbol it’s attached to.
  3. Payload complexity. Each broker needs its own JSON format [SS], and mistakes create wrong sides or sizes.
  4. No evidence yet. Automating an unproven system automates losses faster.

33.4 Setup flow

TRENDSPIDER + SIGNALSTACK STEP — Connect trading [TS][SS]

  1. In TrendSpider, add the Trading Widget to the right sidebar.
  2. Click Enable Trading to connect SignalStack. If you have no SignalStack account, one is created for you.
  3. Confirm that you allow TrendSpider to access your SignalStack account.
  4. In SignalStack, choose Alpaca from the brokers list → Continue → you are redirected to Alpaca → log in → Continue → click Allow to authorise SignalStack.
  5. The account appears under Brokers & Webhooks in SignalStack, and in the TrendSpider Trading widget, usually within a minute.

VERIFY — paper vs live during Alpaca authorisation

SignalStack’s Alpaca guide does not describe how to choose the paper account during OAuth. Your current setup shows an Alpaca Demo/Paper account in TrendSpider. Confirm the exact label you see (e.g., “Demo”, “Paper”) and record it in SS-37. If you also connect a live Alpaca account later, two accounts may appear: always check which is selected.

SECURITY

SignalStack requests access to your entire portfolio to trade [SS]. That is expected. Never paste API keys or passwords into chats, notes or documents, and keep your Alpaca login protected with two-factor authentication.

34 Alpaca Paper Trading

34.1 Account terms as Alpaca shows them

Term Meaning in your paper account
Paper account Simulated account. Default $100,000. Balance cannot be changed after creation; there is no reset button: you open a new paper account instead [ALP]
Portfolio value / equity Cash + positions at current prices. Use this number for the 0.25% calculation.
Cash Uninvested balance (can go negative with margin, and rises when you short)
Buying power Maximum you’re allowed to commit (margin-dependent). Not a sizing target
Positions Current holdings with average entry, market value and unrealized P/L
Orders Every order and its status: new, partially_filled, filled, canceled, expired, rejected, etc. [ALP]
Fill An execution. One order can have several partial fills
Realized P/L Closed-trade profit/loss
Unrealized P/L Open-position mark-to-market

34.2 How paper fills are simulated [ALP]

Aspect Alpaca paper behaviour Real market
Fill price Against the best NBBO price when marketable Depends on depth, queue and speed
Size Not checked against displayed liquidity, so large orders fill fully Large orders move the price
Partial fills ~10% of eligible orders randomly partially fill Common in thin names
Limit orders Fill when the limit reaches the best ask (buy) or bid (sell) You need your queue position to be reached
Market impact, information leakage, latency slippage, price improvement Not modelled Real
Regulatory fees, borrow fees, dividends Not simulated (borrow fees “coming soon”) Real
Market data Paper-only accounts get IEX data only Live accounts may have full SIP data

34.3 Why paper results differ from real trading

Factor Effect
Fills Paper limit orders fill when price merely touches; real ones may not
Slippage Real stops slip more in fast moves
Queue position Real limit orders wait behind earlier orders at the same price
Liquidity / market impact Paper ignores how your order moves price
Latency Real routing and exchange delays
Emotion The largest difference. Losing real money changes behaviour: hesitation, moving stops, revenge trades

PAPER ≠ LIVE

Paper results are an optimistic approximation. A strategy that is only marginally profitable on paper is likely unprofitable live. Never treat paper returns as a forecast of live returns.

VERIFY BEFORE YOUR FIRST REAL SESSION — the 1-share plumbing test

The documentation does not confirm (a) whether a Sell with no position opens a short at Alpaca via SignalStack, (b) whether Stop Loss + Take Profit become a true Alpaca bracket (one cancels the other), and (c) whether a Stop entry can carry Stop Loss / Take Profit. Alpaca itself supports bracket orders with an entry plus a take-profit limit and a stop-loss, where exit legs activate after the entry fills and one cancels the other, during the regular session only [ALP].

Test during market hours with 1 share of a liquid stock (paper):

  1. LONG: Buy 1, Market, Stop Loss and Take Profit set ±$1. Check Alpaca: is it one bracket order with two legs?
  2. Close it from the widget (X). Check that both exit legs were cancelled.
  3. SHORT: Sell 1 (no position), Market, with Stop Loss above and Take Profit below. Check Alpaca: is the position −1?
  4. Stop entry: Buy-Stop 1 share $0.50 above market, with SL/TP. Was it accepted? Cancel it.
  5. Record the results in the Change Log. If any test fails, use the Alpaca dashboard directly for that order type.

35.4 Order types recap

Type Use in v1

35.5 Recommended simplest safe process for v1 paper testing [REC]

Process A — “Confirm then Market” Process B — “Pre-placed Stop entry”
How Watch the trigger. When price trades through it and is within ~0.25R of it, send Market with SL + TP Immediately after the alert, send a Stop entry at the trigger with SL + TP; cancel if not filled within 1–2 candles
Pros No stale orders; works even if Stop+bracket isn’t supported No reaction delay; the entry is mechanical
Cons You must watch; slippage from reaction time Must remember to cancel; depends on the widget supporting Stop + SL/TP
v1 start Use A for the first 10 trades (simplest, fewest moving parts) Move to B after the plumbing test passes and you’re comfortable

36 Tomorrow-Morning Runbook

36.1 Timeline

Time (ET) Action
08:45–09:00 Computer on. TrendSpider logged in. Alpaca paper dashboard open in a second tab. Check that notifications work (phone sound on, TrendSpider app logged in).
09:00–09:15 Note the market context: index futures/pre-market direction, major scheduled news (CPI, FOMC, etc.), any earnings among likely candidates. Write the account equity and today’s $ risk = 0.25% × equity on your sheet.
09:15–09:30 Open the chart layout (5m + 15m). Verify indicator parameters. Delete yesterday’s alerts/lists if not expired. Confirm the Trading widget shows Alpaca PAPER.
09:30–09:40 Observe only. No scans, no trades. Indicators and RVOL are distorted.
~09:40 Run both scanners (Refresh). Rank. Build RB v1 LONG <date> and RB v1 SHORT <date> (≤ 10 each).
09:45–09:55 Create Multi-Factor Alerts on each list (manually or Sidekick: preview → create). Spot-check 2 alerts.

by 15:55 Flat. No overnight positions in v1. Cancel all pending orders.

36.2 When an alert fires — the 17 steps

# Step Detail
1 Open ticker Click the notification or type the symbol.
2 Verify timestamp Alert time vs now. More than ~2 candles old → likely skip.
3 Identify signal candle The 5m candle that closed at the alert time.
4 Check VWAP LONG: close above. SHORT: close below. How far, in ATR units?
5 Check EMA9/EMA20 Aligned? Separation? Slope?
6 Check RSI LONG 55–70 ideal; SHORT 30–45 ideal.
7 Check RVOL > 1.5; not absurd (> 10 = caution).
8 Check 15m confirmation 15m close vs EMA20 on the 15m chart now.
9 Check candle size / extension Range vs ATR; distance from VWAP; Do-Not-Take list.
10 Determine entry LONG: signal high + buffer. SHORT: signal low − buffer.
11 Determine stop LONG: signal low. SHORT: signal high.
12 Risk/share LONG: Entry − Stop. SHORT: Stop − Entry.
13 Quantity min(floor($risk ÷ risk/share), floor(notional cap ÷ entry)).
14 2R target LONG: Entry + 2 × risk/share. SHORT: Entry − 2 × risk/share.
15 Enter PAPER order Process A or B; read the account, side, qty, SL and TP aloud before Submit.
16 Record trade Journal row + “before” screenshot.
17 Monitor exits Stop / 2R / trend failure at each 5m close / time stop at ~30 min.

37 Rapid Execution Cheat Sheet and Position-Size Table

37.1 LONG

Alert → Signal candle → Break HIGH (+buffer) → Stop at LOW → Risk/share → Qty → 2R → Submit

Risk/share = Entry − Stop
Qty        = min( floor($R / Risk/share), floor(Cap / Entry) )
Target     = Entry + 2 × Risk/share

37.2 SHORT

Alert → Signal candle → Break LOW (−buffer) → Stop at HIGH → Risk/share → Qty → 2R → Submit

Risk/share = Stop − Entry
Qty        = min( floor($R / Risk/share), floor(Cap / Entry) )
Target     = Entry − 2 × Risk/share

Where $R = 0.25% × current equity ($250 at $100,000), and Cap = 50% × equity ($50,000) [REC].

37.3 Position-size table ($100,000 account, $250 risk)

Risk/share Shares = floor(250 ÷ risk) Max price before the $50k cap binds*
$0.10 2,500 $20.00
$0.20 1,250 $40.00
$0.25 1,000 $50.00
$0.50 500 $100.00
$0.75 333 $150.15
$1.00 250 $200.00
$1.50 166 $301.20
$2.00 125 $400.00
$2.50 100 $500.00
$5.00 50 $1,000.00

*If the entry price is above this value, use floor($50,000 ÷ entry) instead.

Always round DOWN. 250 ÷ 0.75 = 333.33 → 333, not 334. Rounding up risks more than your limit, and many tiny overshoots add up.

38.2 What matters at 20, 50 and 100 trades

Milestone Purpose Look at Do NOT conclude
20 trades Workflow validation Rules followed %; time from alert to order; sizing errors; order/plumbing errors; slippage per trade Whether the strategy “works”
50 trades Early signal Win rate, average win/loss in R, expectancy, exit-reason mix, R by direction (LONG vs SHORT), R by time of day Final parameter changes
100+ trades More useful evidence Expectancy with confidence range, profit factor, max drawdown, longest losing streak, R by ranking score, time-stop study, Exit C study That live results will match

39 Performance Analysis

39.1 Core metrics

Metric Formula Example (20 trades: 8 wins totalling +14R, 12 losses totalling −12.6R)
Win rate Wins ÷ Trades 8 ÷ 20 = 40%
Loss rate Losses ÷ Trades 60%
Average winner Σ winning R ÷ Wins 14 ÷ 8 = +1.75R
Average loser Σ losing R ÷ Losses −12.6 ÷ 12 = −1.05R
Payoff ratio Avg winner ÷ |Avg loser| 1.75 ÷ 1.05 = 1.67
Expectancy WinRate × AvgWin − LossRate × |AvgLoss| 0.40 × 1.75 − 0.60 × 1.05 = 0.70 − 0.63 = +0.07R
Total R Σ all R 14 − 12.6 = +1.4R (= 20 × 0.07)
Profit factor Gross profit ÷ Gross loss 14 ÷ 12.6 = 1.11
Max drawdown Largest peak-to-trough fall of the equity curve e.g., peak +3.2R → trough −1.8R = 5.0R (≈ $1,250)
Consecutive losses Longest losing streak e.g., 6

Profit factor > 1 = profitable before costs. Most robust intraday systems sit around 1.2–1.8 [IND]. Values > 3 on small samples usually mean luck or overfitting.

39.2 Losing streaks are normal

With a 40% win rate, the probability that any given 6 trades are all losses is 0.6⁶ ≈ 4.7%. Over 100 trades, a 6-loss streak somewhere is likely. At $250 per loss that’s −$1,500 even if the system is profitable. Plan for it emotionally now.

39.3 Sharpe ratio (conceptual)

Sharpe = (average return − risk-free return) ÷ standard deviation of returns. It measures return per unit of volatility. Higher is smoother. For a small sample of trades it is unstable. Use it only once you have months of daily P/L, and prefer expectancy and drawdown at first.

39.4 Statistical traps

Trap Meaning Defence
Small sample 10–20 trades can show almost any result by luck Wait for 100+ trades before strong conclusions
Overfitting Tweaking rules until past results look great; the rules then fit noise Fix rules first; test on unseen data; few parameters
Survivorship bias Testing only on stocks that exist today (today’s S&P 500), ignoring names that were removed (often after falling) Treat backtests on current constituents as optimistic
Look-ahead bias Using information that wasn’t available at decision time (e.g., the day’s final close, a candle’s close before it closed) Current-candle data in the scanner is fine live, but in backtests make sure exits use “After candle closes”
Selection bias Journalling only “good” trades Record every trade and every skipped valid alert

ONE PROFITABLE DAY PROVES ESSENTIALLY NOTHING

A coin-flip system with 2R targets will have many green days. A single day is maybe 0–5 trades: statistically meaningless. Judge the process daily, and the system only after 50–100 trades.

40 Safety and Discipline

Rule Psychological rationale
Paper trade first. Mechanical skill (orders, sizing, speed) must become automatic before money adds stress.
No real-money automation initially. Automation multiplies both edge and errors. You don’t yet know which you have.
Never increase position size to recover a loss. “Getting it back” is loss aversion speaking. Bigger size after losses causes the account-ending day.
Never remove a stop because price approaches it. Hope is not a strategy. The stop is the decision you made while calm.
Never chase a missed entry. FOMO buys late, at worse prices and with larger risk. Another setup will come.
Avoid revenge trading. After a loss, the urge to act immediately produces impulsive, low-quality trades. Use the daily loss limit.
Avoid excessive simultaneous correlated positions. Five tech longs are one big bet. They will stop out together.
Avoid treating one good day as proof. Overconfidence leads to rule-breaking and size creep.
Avoid adjusting parameters until historical results look good. Curve-fitting produces beautiful backtests and poor futures.
Avoid changing strategy mid-session, unless correcting a software/configuration error. Mid-session changes are emotional reactions to the last few trades, and they corrupt your data.

PART VIII — REFERENCE

41 Frequently Asked Questions

41.1 Alerts and signals

1. Why did I receive an alert but price immediately reversed? An alert describes the last closed candle. Many signal candles are the end of a burst. That’s exactly why v1 requires a break of the signal-candle extreme before entry. If price reversed without breaking it, the system worked: you didn’t enter.

2. What if the alert arrives late? Delivery can lag (SMS/email delays, and routing). Check the timestamp. If more than ~2 five-minute candles have passed, or price is > ~0.5R beyond the trigger, skip.

3. Can multiple stocks trigger together? Yes, frequently, especially on strong market moves (they’re correlated). Process them in ranking order and respect the open-risk and position limits.

4. What happens when an alert expires? It stops being checked and won’t fire again. Expirations appear in the Notifications widget [TS]. Expiration counts calendar days [TS].

5. What is the difference between a scanner and an alert? The scanner searches many symbols when you run it and lists candidates. An alert watches one symbol continuously (every 5m close) for a specific setup. Scanner ≠ Alert.

6. Why not simply automate every trade? Because the alert isn’t the whole system. v1 includes human checks (Do-Not-Take list, breakout confirmation), and you have no evidence yet that the system is profitable. Automation magnifies mistakes. Revisit after 100+ journaled trades.

7. Why did my alert fire when my chart doesn’t look like it qualifies? Usual causes: different indicator parameters in the alert vs the chart; the chart is showing extended hours while the alert isn’t (or the reverse); the 15m candle changed after the alert (larger-timeframe conditions can become untrue when that candle closes [TS]); or you are looking at a later candle.

8. Why did my alert not fire although the chart looks perfect? Check: alert expired; conditions are evaluated only at the 5m close [TS]; one condition (often RVOL > 1.5 or Close > Open) failed; Use Extended Hours mismatch; plan alert limit reached.

41.2 Indicators

9. Why is RSI 75 not automatically a SHORT? RSI 75 means buyers have dominated recently: that’s momentum, not a reversal signal. v1 shorts require price below VWAP, EMA9 < EMA20 and RSI < 45.

10. Why can RVOL be 12 at the close? The closing auction and end-of-day rebalancing create huge volume in the final minutes. Compared with the prior 20 quieter bars, the ratio explodes. It’s normal and not a v1 signal.

11. Why does TrendSpider show post-market RVOL? If extended hours are shown on the chart, post-market bars have volume, and thin bars make ratios swing wildly. v1 ignores extended-hours readings.

12. What does “last” mean? The price of the most recent trade. It isn’t necessarily the price you can buy (ask) or sell (bid) at.

13. What does “1 candle ago” mean? The previous candle on that condition’s timeframe: on 5m, the previous 5-minute bar; on Daily, the previous trading day.

14. Why is EMA9 below EMA20? Recent prices (weighted heavily in EMA9) are lower than the medium-term average, so the short-term trend is down. For a LONG that disqualifies the setup.

15. What if price is above VWAP but RSI is weak (e.g., 50)? Fails v1 (RSI must be > 55). Price may be drifting above VWAP without momentum, which is common in chop.

16. What if 5m is bullish but 15m is bearish? No LONG (fails condition 6). The 5m move is likely a counter-trend bounce into higher-timeframe sellers.

17. Why does my VWAP differ from someone else’s? Different settings: session vs anchored, extended hours included or not, price source (HLC3 vs Close), and possibly the Length setting (see the Chapter 3 VERIFY box).

18. Is “overbought” a reason to exit a LONG? Not in v1. Exits are A–D only. Overextension matters at entry (ranking/Do-Not-Take), not as an exit.

41.3 Entries and stops

19. What if the entry candle is huge? Range > ~2× the 5m ATR → skip. The stop is far, and the candle may be exhaustion.

20. What if I miss the breakout? Skip. If price has moved > ~0.5R beyond the trigger, your planned risk/reward no longer exists.

21. What if the stop is too far away? Skip the trade, or accept the smaller share count that the formula gives. Never move the stop closer artificially.

22. What if the stock hits my target immediately? Great: the limit fills, and you record +2R (minus slippage). Don’t re-enter impulsively. Wait for a new alert.

23. Should I move my stop to break-even? Not in v1. Break-even stops are a v2 test item, to be evaluated with data.

24. Why must I wait 1–2 candles at most? Your rule. Momentum setups are perishable. A setup that doesn’t confirm quickly has a lower probability. This is a trading rule, not a TrendSpider limitation.

25. What buffer should I use above the high? $0.01–$0.05 for most stocks; up to ~$0.10 for $200–$500 stocks [REC]. Be consistent and journal it.

26. Can I enter before the break to get a better price? That’s a different strategy (anticipation). Not v1.

27. What if the signal candle is tiny? The stop becomes tiny, size becomes huge (the cap binds), and the spread is a big share of risk. Consider skipping (Do-Not-Take item 11).

41.4 Risk and sizing

28. How many positions should I hold? Recommendation: max 2 during the first 20 trades, then 3–4, with total open risk ≤ 1% of equity.

29. Why is share quantity an output? Because the risk is fixed first ($250), and the stop is fixed by structure. The quantity is whatever makes those two consistent.

30. Why round down? Rounding up exceeds your risk limit.

31. Should I risk more on “A+” setups? Not in v1. Variable sizing requires evidence that your grading predicts outcomes (Chapter 15 rubric, after 100 trades).

32. Does the 0.25% use starting or current equity? Current equity, recalculated at least daily (each morning).

33. What is a daily loss limit? A pre-set loss at which you stop for the day (recommendation: −1% or 3 consecutive losses).

41.5 Orders, brokers and accounts

34. What is buying power? The maximum dollar amount the broker allows you to commit now. It isn’t a target and doesn’t change your risk rules.

35. Why does paper trading differ from real trading? Simulated fills (no queue, no market impact, size not checked against liquidity), different data (IEX for paper-only accounts), no fees, and no real emotions [ALP].

36. Why did my order not fill? A limit/stop price was never reached; a limit order was beyond the market; it was rejected (check Alpaca: buying power, sub-penny price, extended-hours rules [ALP]); or it was cancelled at end of day (TIF day).

37. What is a stop-limit? A stop that, when triggered, sends a limit order instead of a market order. It protects price but may not fill. The TrendSpider widget documents only Market/Limit/Stop [TS].

38. What does “market closed” mean? The regular session (09:30–16:00 ET) isn’t running. Market orders may be rejected or queued. Extended-hours orders at Alpaca must be limit orders [ALP].

39. Why did my order get rejected for price? Prices ≥ $1 must use at most 2 decimals [ALP]. $100.205 is invalid.

40. Do short sales work in my paper account? Alpaca supports shorting in paper [ALP]. Whether the TrendSpider widget’s “Sell” opens a short via SignalStack must be confirmed with the 1-share test (Chapter 35).

41. What is the SSR? Short Sale Restriction (SEC Rule 201): after a ≥ 10% drop from the prior close, shorts may only execute above the national best bid for the rest of that day and the next [REG]. v1 recommendation: skip shorts in SSR names.

42. Is the PDT rule still a problem? FINRA’s amended Rule 4210 removed the PDT designation and the $25,000 minimum effective June 4, 2026, replaced by intraday margin requirements (brokers may phase in until Oct 20, 2027) [REG]. Confirm your broker’s implementation before going live.

43. Why don’t I see my executed order in TrendSpider? The Trading widget does not display executed orders [TS]. Check Open Positions (may lag up to 1 minute) and the Alpaca dashboard.

44. Does a paper order use SignalStack signals? SignalStack’s pricing lists unlimited paper signals [SS]. VERIFY any TrendSpider-side limits.

41.6 TrendSpider usage

45. Why do scanner results change every few minutes? With Current Candle ON, the forming candle counts as if closed [TS]. Stocks drift in and out until the candle closes.

46. Why doesn’t my scanner update by itself? Scans don’t auto-refresh. Use Refresh Scan Results [TS].

47. Can Sidekick place trades? No. Sidekick cannot place, modify or close trades; its SignalStack connection is read-only [TS].

48. How many alerts can I have? It depends on your plan (10 / 50 / 100 / 400 by tier on the pricing page checked 2026-10-28). VERIFY in your account.

49. Can I alert on the 1-minute chart? No. The lowest alert timeframe is 5 minutes [TS].

50. Can I backtest the exact v1 system? Not exactly: the Strategy Tester uses one timeframe and can’t express the breakout entry or the candle-based stop natively. See Chapter 31 for the closest approximation.

51. Why is the “Chg%” column different from my 1% condition? Columns may compute change against a different reference (e.g., including extended-hours prices, or relative to the open), and the scanner uses the price at scan time. Verify by comparing the daily chart’s previous close.

52. Should I trade the first 10 minutes? Not in v1. Observe only, 09:30–09:40.

53. Can I trade pre-market with v1? No. v1 is regular-session only. A pre-market system would need different scanners (Chapter 25) and limit-only orders.

54. What if TrendSpider and Alpaca prices differ slightly? Data feeds differ (Alpaca paper-only accounts use IEX data [ALP]). Small differences are normal. Base decisions on TrendSpider, confirm fills in Alpaca.

55. How long until I know whether v1 works? Expect 100+ trades. At 2–3 trades per day, that’s roughly 2–3 months of paper trading.

42 Troubleshooting

Symptom Likely cause Fix
Scanner returns too many stocks Strong market day; Current Candle mid-bar; thresholds loose Rank and keep the top 10; re-scan after the candle closes; don’t loosen v1 to fix it
Scanner count increases after tightening a condition The scan ran at a different moment (Current Candle ON); or the edit changed AND to Any/OR; or a condition’s timeframe changed Check the group is All of the following; check each condition’s timeframe; re-run twice at the same candle
Displayed Chg% does not match the scanner condition Different reference price (extended-hours close, open), or timing Trust the condition; verify on the daily chart
Alert does not fire Expired; a condition not met at the 5m close; Use Extended Hours mismatch; plan alert limit hit; on the wrong symbol Open the alert and check each condition on the chart at the last closed 5m candle
SMS does not arrive Wrong number; do-not-disturb window; weekend setting; carrier delay Account & Settings → Notifications; test with a throwaway alert
Sidekick sees the wrong watchlist Ambiguous name; several lists with similar names Use the exact list name; date-stamp lists; “my list” triggers a dropdown picker [TS]
Sidekick created unexpected alerts Prompt too vague Delete them; always use preview → create
Trading widget shows the live account instead of paper Wrong brokerage selected; multiple Alpaca connections Select the PAPER account; consider not connecting live until needed
SignalStack cannot see Alpaca Authorisation not completed; expired token; wrong Alpaca login Re-run SignalStack → Alpaca connect (Allow); check Brokers & Webhooks
Order rejected Insufficient buying power; sub-penny price; extended-hours order not limit; shorting not available Check the Alpaca order’s rejection reason [ALP]
Stop Loss field unavailable That order type/broker combination doesn’t support attached exits; widget beta Place the stop as a separate order in Alpaca; record in the Change Log
VWAP parameter differs between chart and alert Edited one but not the other Re-create the alert from a saved template with the correct parameters
RVOL unexpectedly huge Opening/closing bars; news; halt; extended-hours bars Ignore during 09:30–09:40 and after 15:45; check news
Scanner results differ after hours Ext. Hours setting; data now includes post-market; Current Candle on a closed session Run v1 scans during the regular session only
Position shows but stop/target missing Exit legs not created or cancelled Immediately add the stop in Alpaca; investigate
Unexpected new position after a manual close An orphaned stop/target leg filled Cancel all pending orders after every manual exit
Chart and alert disagree on 15m 15m candle still forming at alert time Re-check the 15m at its close
Paper P/L looks too good No slippage/queue modelling Add a slippage estimate to the journal; be conservative

LONG SHORT

Target Entry + 2 × risk Entry − 2 × risk

43.6 Sheet 6 — Risk calculator

$R      = 0.0025 × equity                  (100,000 → 250)
Shares  = floor($R / risk_per_share)
Cap     = floor(0.50 × equity / entry)     [REC]
Qty     = min(Shares, Cap)
Risk $  = Qty × risk_per_share

Need Where [TS]

43.8 Sheet 8 — Scanner workflow

  1. 09:40 Refresh both scanners (Current Candle ✓, Ext. Hours ☐, S&P 500).
  2. Rank (RVOL, VWAP distance in ATR, EMA separation, RSI zone, daily %, 15m, extension).
  3. Keep the top ≤ 10 per side → static lists RB v1 LONG/SHORT <date>.
  4. Re-scan at 11:00 and 13:30; update the lists.

43.9 Sheet 9 — Alert workflow

  1. Preview, then create the LONG alerts on the LONG list and the SHORT alerts on the SHORT list (≤ 20 per Sidekick message).
  2. Expiry: end of day. Regular hours only.

  4. When one fires → the 17-step procedure.

43.10 Sheet 10 — Paper-order workflow

  1. Widget account = Alpaca PAPER.
  2. Side: Buy (LONG) / Sell (SHORT).
  3. Type: Market after the trigger trades (Process A) or Stop at the trigger (Process B).
  4. Qty = calculator.
  5. Stop Loss = signal extreme; Take Profit = 2R.
  6. Read aloud → Submit → confirm in Alpaca → journal.

43.11 Sheet 11 — Daily routine

08:45 setup → 09:00 context and $R → 09:15 verify charts and account → 09:30 observe → 09:40 scan/rank/lists → 09:45 alerts → 10:00–15:30 trade → 11:00 and 13:30 re-scan → 15:30 no new entries → 15:55 flat → 16:00 review.

43.12 Sheet 12 — End-of-day review

  • Any software/configuration issue → Change Log.

44 Am I Ready for Live Trading?

This checklist requires EVIDENCE, not confidence. Every box must be ticked from your journal. If any box is unticked, the answer is no: keep paper trading. Passing it does not guarantee live profitability.

# Requirement Evidence ☐
1 ≥ 100 paper trades under the same rule version Journal count ☐
2 Spanning ≥ 2 calendar months and different market conditions (up, down and choppy days) Dates, regime tags ☐
3 Expectancy > +0.15R per trade after a conservative slippage adjustment (e.g., subtract 0.1R per trade) Spreadsheet ☐
4 Profit factor ≥ 1.3 Spreadsheet ☐
5 Max drawdown ≤ 10R, and you continued following rules through it Equity curve ☐
6 Rules followed on ≥ 95% of trades in the last 50 “Followed rules?” column ☐
7 Zero sizing errors and zero “wrong account” incidents in the last 50 trades Journal ☐
8 Both LONG and SHORT reviewed separately. Trade only the side(s) that are positive on their own Split stats ☐
9 Results not dependent on 1–3 outlier trades (remove the top 3 winners → still ≥ 0R) Spreadsheet ☐
10 A written plan for live: starting size ¼ of paper risk (e.g., 0.0625%), daily loss limit, max positions Change Log entry ☐
11 Broker rules understood (intraday margin under amended FINRA 4210, short availability, fees) Notes ☐
12 Order plumbing tested on the live account with minimum size Test log ☐
13 No unresolved VERIFY items affecting execution (Chapter 35 tests passed) Appendix C / Change Log ☐
14 You have pre-decided what result would make you stop live trading (e.g., −15R or 30 trades below expectations) Written ☐

APPENDICES

Appendix A — Glossary

Term Definition
ADR (Average Daily Range) Average of (daily high − daily low) over N days; how far a stock typically travels in a day.
ADX Average Directional Index; measures trend strength (0–100), not direction.
After-hours (post-market) 16:00–20:00 ET trading session.
Alert A rule that watches a symbol and notifies you when its conditions are met. Not a trade.
Alpaca Brokerage offering an API and a free paper-trading environment.
Anchored VWAP (AVWAP) VWAP calculated from a user-chosen starting candle.
AND logic All conditions must be true (“All of the following”).
Ask (offer) Lowest price a seller currently accepts.
ATR (Average True Range) Smoothed average of true range; a volatility measure.
Average volume Mean volume over N periods.
Backtest Simulating a strategy on historical data.
Base (RVOL) Reference level of the Relative Volume indicator (1 = average volume).
Bearish Expecting or showing falling prices.
Bid Highest price a buyer currently pays.
Body (candle) Part of a candle between open and close.
Bracket order Entry order with attached stop-loss and take-profit; one exit cancels the other.
Break-even stop Stop moved to the entry price after a gain. Not in v1.
Breakdown Price moving below support.
Breakout Price moving above resistance.
Breakout candle Candle that closes beyond a key level.
Bullish Expecting or showing rising prices.
Buy to cover Buying shares to close a short position.
Buying power Maximum amount the broker lets you commit now.
Candle (candlestick) Visual summary of open, high, low and close for one period.
Candle range High − Low.
Cash Uninvested account balance.
Chasing Entering after price has already moved well beyond the planned entry.
Close Last price of a period.
Commission Broker fee per trade (Alpaca: commission-free stock trading; regulatory fees may apply live).
Concentration Large exposure to one name, sector or theme.
Condition group Set of conditions combined with All/Any/None logic in TrendSpider.
Consolidation Sideways, range-bound price action.
Constant value A fixed number used in a condition (e.g., RSI > 55).
Correlation Tendency of two instruments to move together.
Current Candle (scanner) TrendSpider option to evaluate the forming candle as if closed.
Day trade Opening and closing a position in the same session.
Depth (Strategy Tester) Number of candles or date range used in a backtest.
Divergence Price and an indicator moving in opposite directions.
Doji Candle with open ≈ close; indecision.
Drawdown Decline from an equity peak to a subsequent trough.
EMA (Exponential Moving Average) Moving average weighting recent prices more heavily; α = 2/(N+1).
EMA alignment Relative position of EMAs (e.g., EMA9 above EMA20).
EMA crossover Event when one EMA crosses another.
Engulfing (bullish/bearish) Two-candle pattern in which the second body covers the first.
Entry Price where a position is opened.
Equity (portfolio value) Cash plus the market value of positions.
Exit Price where a position is closed.
Expectancy Average result per trade: Win% × AvgWin − Loss% × AvgLoss.
Expiration (alert) When an alert stops being active (time or trigger count).
Extended hours Pre-market and after-hours sessions.
Fill Execution of an order (fully or partially).
FOMO Fear of missing out; leads to chasing.
Gap Open far from the prior close, leaving empty space on the chart.
Gap risk Risk that price jumps past your stop.
Hammer Small body near the top with a long lower wick; potential reversal at support.
Happened / Happened Within TrendSpider condition timing: exact candle vs within N candles.
High Highest price of a period.
HLC3 (High + Low + Close) ÷ 3; typical price.
Inside bar Candle whose range lies within the prior candle’s range.
Intraday margin FINRA 4210 standard (effective 2026-06-04) replacing PDT rules for margin accounts.
Inverted hammer Small body near the bottom with a long upper wick after a decline.
Last Most recent trade price.
Length Number of periods used by an indicator.
Limit order Order to trade at a specified price or better.
Liquidity Ease of trading without moving the price.
Locate Broker confirmation that shares can be borrowed for a short sale.
Long Owning shares; profits if price rises.
Look-ahead bias Using information not yet available at decision time.
Low Lowest price of a period.
MA Type Averaging method (SMA, EMA, HullMA…).
MACD EMA12 − EMA26 with a signal line; momentum indicator.
MAE Maximum adverse excursion: worst unrealised loss during a trade.
Margin Borrowing from the broker; required for shorting.
Market order Order to trade immediately at the best available price.
Market Scanner TrendSpider tool that screens many symbols against conditions.
Mean reversion Tendency of stretched prices to return toward an average.
MFE Maximum favourable excursion: best unrealised gain during a trade.
Momentum Speed and persistence of price movement.
Multi-Factor Alert TrendSpider alert combining several conditions/timeframes.
NBBO National Best Bid and Offer.
Notional Shares × price; the position’s dollar size.
OCO One-Cancels-Other pair of exit orders.
Offset Candle reference: 0 current, −1 previous.
OHLC Open, High, Low, Close.
Open First price of a period.
Open risk Sum of the risk of all open positions.
OR logic Any condition true (“Any of the following”).
Overextension Price stretched far from its averages.
Overfitting Tuning rules to past noise.
Paper trading Simulated trading with no real money.
Partial profit Closing part of a position early. Not in v1.
Payoff ratio Average win ÷ average loss.
PDT (Pattern Day Trader) Former FINRA designation with a $25,000 minimum; removed effective 2026-06-04.
Pivot points Levels calculated from the prior day’s H, L, C.
Position Current holding in a symbol (+ long, − short).
Position Tool TrendSpider drawing showing entry/stop/target zones.
Pre-market 04:00–09:30 ET session.
Price Source Candle value an indicator uses (Close, HLC3…).
Profit factor Gross profit ÷ gross loss.
Pullback Temporary move against the prevailing trend.
R (R-multiple) Result expressed in units of initial risk.
Realized P/L Profit/loss on closed positions.
Regular market hours 09:30–16:00 ET.
Rejection candle Candle that pierces a level but closes back on the original side.
Relative Strength (RS) Performance vs a benchmark (not RSI).
Resistance Zone where rallies have repeatedly stalled.
Retest Return to a broken level from the other side.
Reversal Change in trend direction.
Revenge trading Impulsive trading to recover losses.
Risk per share Distance from entry to stop.
Risk/reward Potential reward ÷ potential risk.
RSI (Relative Strength Index) 0–100 momentum oscillator: 100 − 100/(1 + RS).
RVOL (Relative Volume) Volume ÷ its moving average.
Scanner Tool that finds candidates across many symbols.
Sharpe ratio Excess return ÷ volatility of returns.
Short (short sale) Selling borrowed shares; profits if price falls.
Shooting star Long upper wick and small low body after an advance.
Sidekick TrendSpider’s AI assistant.
Signal (SignalStack) An order successfully sent to a linked broker.
Signal candle The completed 5m candle that satisfied the alert.
SignalStack Order-routing service connecting TrendSpider to brokers.
Slippage Difference between the planned and actual fill.
SMA (Simple Moving Average) Equal-weighted average of N closes.
Smart Watchlist Saved scan used as a re-runnable watchlist.
Spread Ask − Bid.
SSR (Short Sale Restriction) Rule 201 restriction after a ≥ 10% drop from the prior close.
Static watchlist Fixed list of symbols.
Stochastic Oscillator showing the close’s position within the recent range.
Stop order Becomes a market order when the stop price trades.
Stop-limit order Becomes a limit order when the stop price trades.
Stop-loss Pre-set exit that limits the loss.
Strategy Tester TrendSpider’s backtesting tool.
Support Zone where declines have repeatedly stalled.
Survivorship bias Ignoring instruments that disappeared.
Take-profit Pre-set exit that captures a gain.
TIF (Time in Force) How long an order stays active (day, gtc, ioc, fok…).
Time stop Exit after a set time without sufficient progress.
Timeframe Period that one candle represents.
Trading widget TrendSpider’s order ticket using SignalStack.
Trailing stop Stop that follows price at a set distance. Not in v1.
Trend Persistent directional movement.
True Range max(H − L, |H − prev C|, |L − prev C|).
Unrealized P/L Profit/loss on open positions.
Visual Scripts TrendSpider’s condition-building and template system.
Volatility Size of price fluctuations.
Volume Number of shares traded.
VWAP Volume Weighted Average Price: Σ(TP × V) ÷ ΣV.
VWAP reclaim / rejection Close back above VWAP / failure at VWAP.
Watchlist List of symbols to monitor.
Webhook Automated HTTP message sent when an alert fires. Not used in v1.
Whipsaw Rapid false signals in choppy markets.
Win rate Winning trades ÷ total trades.
